statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-115207: when GNU patch reverse-applies a patch that deletes a file (for example when, in batch mode, it finds that the file to delete does not exist and assumes -R), it created that file without checking that its name is safe, so a crafted patch naming an absolute or ../ path could create a file outside the working directory with the permissions of the user running patch. Upstream fixed it in commit 0cd45bb ("Prevent creation of out-of-tree files (CVE-2026-115207)"), released in patch 2.8.1, and Debian fixed trixie in 2.8-2+deb13u1: https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/patch.git/commit/?id=0cd45bb2132a42cd38d84b20661f3eae9b4da7ce, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115207. The DHI patch package for Debian 13 is built from Debian's patch 2.8-2 source with that upstream change backported. The only patch build published in the DHI Debian repository for Debian 13 (amd64 and arm64, with its patch-dbgsym), the version this range marks as fixed, records the backport of the CVE-2026-115207 fix in its shipped changelog. Ran the shipped /usr/bin/patch from both the amd64 and the arm64 package with -t against a patch that deletes a nonexistent file at an absolute path outside the working directory: it prints "Ignoring potentially dangerous file name" and creates nothing, while Debian's unfixed patch 2.8-2 binary, run the same way, assumes -R and creates the file. The DHI build also prints that warning for the ../g case in the upstream tests/bad-filenames test that the fix commit updates, and Debian's 2.8-2 binary does not.
